title: Introduce anticipatory throughput conservation and hybrid probe scheduler
author: Aisha Patel
ci_status: pass (first CI run had a flaky prober integration test failure; rerun passed)
description:
Motivation: Production canary evaluations occasionally cause short-lived throughput spikes that bias regression detectors and trigger noisy rollbacks. This PR introduces an anticipatory throughput conservation mechanism paired with a hybrid probe scheduler to reduce probe-induced perturbation while preserving detection sensitivity.

What this does: Adds a lightweight tokenized credit-bank (burst credit) that conserves headroom for real traffic by smoothing synthetic probe injections and limiting their instantaneous weight. Implements a hybrid probe scheduler that mixes low-cost micro-probes (short requests targeting tail latency) with scheduled macro-probes (full-stack traffic slices) and routes probes through a conservative queuing path to avoid saturating shared worker pools.

Key components included: 1) conservation/credit-bank service (inproc sharded module) that tracks per-replica and per-cluster credits, refills credits using traffic-aware budgeting, and exposes a diagnostics endpoint; 2) hybrid_probe_scheduler that orchestrates micro vs macro probes and supports pluggable sampling policies; 3) probe-router conservative path that applies soft-priority throttling and falls back to shadow routing when pressure is detected; 4) metrics and tagging additions for canary dashboards (probe.type, conservation.credit_balance, probe.inhibited_reason).

Algorithm summary: - Credit refill rate is proportional to recent sustained client throughput with a configurable min refill floor to keep sensitivity. - Probe weight is normalized by expected per-replica capacity; attempts to allocate credits atomically and fails fast if insufficient credits exist. - When queue-depth or CPU utilization crosses SLO thresholds, the scheduler reduces macro-probe rate and increases micro-probe frequency to maintain diagnostic coverage without causing degradation.

Testing and validation: - Unit tests for credit accounting and scheduler policies. - Synthetic load test harness that simulates 3 traffic modes (steady, bursty, diurnal) and compares canary signal stability vs baseline (no conservation). Results in /perf-canary/test-results/summary show 42% reduction in false-positive regressions under bursty traffic and <2% reduction in true-positive detection rate. - End-to-end staging canary run with 48h burn; dashboards included in screenshots and CSV in branch.

Rollout plan: Feature gated behind config flag perf.canary.conservation.enabled (default: off). We enable in staging for two weeks, then enable progressively in low-traffic clusters (10% of production) with monitoring alarms for credit starvation and probe suppression. Auto-disable on sustained probe.inhibited_reason == "RESOURCE_PRESSURE" for >5 minutes.

Backward compatibility: All APIs are additive. When disabled, scheduler behaves identically to existing prober. No changes to public RPCs for external services.

Related: ENG-9334 (canary noise reduction), ENG-9401 (probe scheduler refactor).

release_notes: Add anticipatory throughput conservation and hybrid probe scheduler to reduce probe-induced canary noise. Feature is disabled by default and gated behind perf.canary.conservation.enabled. See canary-runbook.md for rollout steps.
notes_for_ops: Watch metrics: conservation.credit_balance (per-replica), probe.inhibited_reason, prober.pending_queue_depth. If credit_balance stays at zero for >10 minutes across >50% replicas, disable feature and investigate autoscaler or traffic-routing anomalies.
manual_backout_steps: Flip perf.canary.conservation.enabled=false in config service; if control-plane unavailable, set probe.scheduler.rate_limit=0 in per-cluster overrides and restart prober service.
